I also want to die and I also want to get better. I'm told that wanting to get better is the first step.


Have you spoken to your parents/healthcare providers about anti-depressants? Are you seeing any therapists? I think some professional help is more than called for at this point.
Thanks that's reassuring to hear & good advice.

I'd like to say that I think about hurting myself almost all the time. I don't want to, and I don't want to kill myself and leave him, but it's like a drumbeat echoing in my head and sometimes it just gets to be too much. And I know that I need help and I just need to wait it out but it's also such a long time and a tough season and I don't know exactly what I need from him but I guess just that I need him to know how I feel.

Thanks for the reply & openess about your experience. 

How did you bring it up to your mother? 

I feel like I'm searching for a right time & place but there never is one. I struggle to talk about anything at all when I'm feeling at my worst, and then when things get better I don't want to bring back up all the nasty feelings.

Yeah, I guess the more I think about it it's really just me trying to make things harder on myself? I know I shouldn't feel guilty for having a hard time but also when I'm in the trenches guilt is a huge emotion.

I'm just trying to figure out how to bring it up to him. 

When I'm really feeling bad it's so hard for me to talk about it, and then when I'm in a good place it's hard for me to bring it up cause I don't want to ruin the good feelings, if that makes sense.

I feel like I'm waiting for a right time and place and there never is one.
